newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea blames Seoul for Red Cross talks failure.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea blames Seoul for Red Cross talks failure.

text.p: North Korea on Tuesday blamed an "eccentric and incomprehensible" attitude by South Korea for the failure of Red Cross organisations of the two countries to agree on shipments of food aid to famine-hit North Korea.

The official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), monitored in Tokyo, quoted a North Korean Red Cross official as saying Seoul had failed to make clear what food aid it would offer and when the aid would be delivered.
Negotiations on speeding up food aid to North Korea began last Friday in Beijing and broke down on Monday. They were the first such inter-Korean Red Cross talks in almost five years.

"But no agreement was reached at the contact (meeting) due to the south side's eccentric and incomprehensible attitude," KCNA said, quoting what it said was an unnamed spokesman for the North Korean Red Cross.
"The south side insisted on the discussion of the procedures and method of the offering, not making clear what they will offer to the north and when. It is really unreasonable."

But the spokesman left open the possibility of further talks, saying: "We will meet with the south side anytime when it notifies us of the date of the contact after preparing the relief goods in a responsible manner."
